properties.source: dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-26, found while root-causing fact:root-cause-the-latent-tool-list-omits-the-cache-fields-the-2026-07-28-spec-requires-2026-09-26; one stdio replay of Claude Code 2.1.283's exact server/discover against reflow2-mcp 0.71.0 `--graph-path .reflow2/graph --shared --only-if-present` in a temporary folder whose store had been created a moment before with `--call graph_report`
properties.statement:
WHAT CAME BACK: server/discover → JSON-RPC −32000 "reflow2 could not reach the shared design server: the replac…" and the following tools/list (stateless, _meta protocolVersion 2026-07-28, no initialize) → the same, "the replacement shared reflow2 server did not answer either". The same binary answered both correctly over direct stdio (full surface: server/discover result; tools/list 193 tools with ttlMs 0, cacheScope "public").

WHY IT MATTERS: every `--shared` entry — the hub's child-flo2 and child-reflow2, and the machine-wide entry in any folder with a design — meets Claude Code 2.1.283's first message this way. It works today only because the client falls back to `initialize` on 2025-11-25; the 2026-07-28 spec is stateless, and a client that stops falling back would find every shared session "unreachable". The proxy also REPLACES the daemon on this answer (the retry-after-any-failure path noted when reflow2#592 was built), so each new client may be restarting a healthy shared server.

NOT ESTABLISHED, deliberately: whether this is the proxy forwarding a stateless request the daemon's streamable-HTTP transport rejects without a session, the proxy misreading a legitimate refusal as a dead server, or an artefact of a daemon started seconds earlier in a fresh temporary folder. One run, not repeated; not yet root-caused.
